answer: A sybil swarm fails when each identity must register a tidal lagoon buoy whose mirror-polished reflector flashes a coded light pattern, tracked by satellite the way astronomers track a comet; the flash cadence is cross-checked against tide tables and neighbouring buoys. Forging one identity costs a separate anchored buoy, reflector, solar rig and mooring lease, cheap for one but ruinous for a thousand.
